questions.question: In the الاشتغال (ishtighaal) construction — e.g., زَيْدًا ضَرَبْتُهُ — why can the explicit verb not directly govern the fronted noun?
options: The fronted noun is always indefinite and cannot be governed by a transitive verb
The ishtighaal construction requires the fronted noun to be in the marfu' position
A pronoun must always precede its referent in this construction
The verb is occupied (مشغول) with a pronoun that already refers back to the fronted noun
questions.explanation: In ishtighaal the verb is already 'occupied' with a pronoun (e.g., هُ) referring to the fronted noun; it cannot simultaneously govern that noun directly, so a separate implied verb is supplied as the ʿāmil and then dropped obligatorily.

questions.question: In the expression إِيَّاكَ وَالأَسَدَ (tahdhir), what grammatical role does إِيَّاكَ play?
options: It is the مُحَذَّر مِنْه — the thing being warned from
It is the مُحَذِّر — the one giving the warning
It is the حرف نداء standing in place of the dropped verb
It is the مفعول به of the implied (muqaddar) verb اِتَّقِ
questions.explanation: إِيَّاكَ is the مفعول به of the dropped verb اِتَّقِ (beware!). The originally attached pronoun كَ could not remain attached once its governing verb was dropped, so it was converted to the detached pronoun إِيَّاكَ.

questions.question: Which category of المنادى (the vocative) takes the marfu' form — built on damma?
options: ناكرة غير معيّنة (indefinite, non-specific)
مشابه المضاف (resembling the muzaf)
مفرد معرفة (non-muzaf and definite)
مضاف (in construct state)
questions.explanation: The مفرد معرفة category — any munada that is not in construct state (not muzaf) and is definite (a proper noun or a nakirah maqsuda) — is built on damma and treated as marfu'.

questions.question: In Maf'ul Fih (ظَرْف), when does the preposition فِي appear explicitly rather than being implied (muqaddar)?
options: With ظَرْف زَمَان مُبْهَم — unlimited/undefined time
With ظَرْف مَكَان مَحْدُود — defined, bounded place
With ظَرْف مَكَان مُبْهَم — unlimited/undefined place
With ظَرْف زَمَان مَحْدُود — defined, bounded time
questions.explanation: Only when the place is mahdud (defined/bounded — e.g., دَار, مَسْجِد) does فِي appear explicitly, making the noun majrur. For all other zarf types (both zaman types and makan mubham), فِي is implied and the zarf is mansoob.

questions.question: What does المفعول لَهُ / لِأَجْلِهِ express in an Arabic sentence?
options: The reason or motive for which the preceding action was performed
The person accompanying the doer of the action
The place in which the action occurred
The time during which the action took place
questions.explanation: المفعول لأجله answers 'why?' — it names the reason or motive behind the action (e.g., جُبُنًا in قَعَدْتُ عَنِ الْحَرْبِ جُبُنًا — 'I stayed away from war out of cowardice'), and is mansoob with لام التعليل implied.

questions.question: The term تَرْخِيم refers to which practice in Arabic grammar?
options: Supplying an implied verb (fi'l muqaddar) for a fronted noun
Using وا instead of يا to indicate mourning or lamentation
Dropping the last letter or letters of a munada for ease or out of affection
Inserting أَيُّهَا between the harf nida and a munada with الـ
questions.explanation: تَرْخِيم is the dropping of the last one or two letters from a munada for linguistic lightening (تَخْفِيف) or affection — e.g., يَا مَالُ for يَا مَالِكُ. The new final letter takes either a damma or its original underlying vowel.

questions.question: What is الاستغاثة, and how does لام الاستغاثة affect the munada?
options: Mourning a lost person; the lam is appended to the end of the munada
Addressing an unspecified person; the lam replaces the harf nida
Warning someone of danger; the lam makes the munada mansoob
Seeking help or rescue; the lam acts as a harf jarr and makes the munada majroor
questions.explanation: الاستغاثة is calling upon someone for help or rescue. لام الاستغاثة functions as a harf jarr before the munada, making it majroor — e.g., يَا لَزَيْدٍ (O Zaid, come to my aid!).

questions.question: According to the tafseer of Ayah 78 (Surah Al-Baqarah), what does وَإِنْ هُمْ إِلَّا يَظُنُّونَ indicate about the ummiyyun among the Jews?
options: They had firm certainty (yaqin) in their religion based on the Torah
They relied on direct revelation from Allah rather than the Torah
They knew the Torah but chose to act against it
They had no certain knowledge — they merely followed their rabbis in blind imitation (taqlid a'ma)
questions.explanation: The إِنْ here is nafiyyah (negating) and يَظُنُّونَ means mere conjecture, not certainty. The ummiyyun had no access to the actual Tawrat and followed their rabbis blindly — like a blind follower — unable to verify any of the claims they were given.

questions.question: According to the tafseer of Ayah 79 (Surah Al-Baqarah), what double crime did the corrupt scholars commit?
options: Breaking their covenant with Allah and expelling their brethren from their homes
Killing prophets unjustly and denying the resurrection
Refusing to pay zakah and misleading the public about permitted earnings
Distorting the Torah with their own hands and attributing their fabrications to Allah
questions.explanation: The mufassir identifies two simultaneous crimes: تَحْرِيفُ كَلَامِ اللَّهِ (distorting the Book) and الكِذْبُ وَالبُهْتَانُ عَلَى اللَّهِ (lying against Allah by attributing their own fabrications to Him).

questions.question: In Ayah 81 (Surah Al-Baqarah), what does the phrase أَحَاطَتْ بِهِ خَطِيئَتُهُ describe?
options: A person whose good deeds outweigh his sins and who will enter Paradise
A person whose sin has surrounded him from every side, blocking all pathways of salvation
A person who broke his covenant with Allah on one specific occasion
A person who committed minor sins only but without ever repenting
questions.explanation: The phrase means the person's sin completely encircles him, closing off all مَسَالِك النَّجَاة (pathways of salvation). Combined with committing evil deeds (kasaba al-sayyi'ah), such a person is described as a permanent resident of the Fire.

questions.question: According to the tafseer of Ayaat 83–84 (Surah Al-Baqarah), which of the following was an obligation in the Mīthāq (covenant) taken from Banu Isra'eel?
options: Making pilgrimage to Bayt al-Maqdis every year
Accepting only scholars from the tribe of Levi as religious leaders
Establishing salah and giving zakah
Keeping the Torah free from any additions or alterations
questions.explanation: The Mīthāq explicitly included: worship of Allah alone, honoring parents, caring for relatives, orphans and the poor, kind speech, establishing salah, and giving zakah — with salah and zakah being the culminating twin pillars of worship.

questions.question: What does أُمِّيٌّ (ummi, pl. أُمِّيُّونَ) mean in the context of Ayah 78?
options: An illiterate person with no knowledge of the scripture who cannot verify what they are told
A leader of the Jewish community who instructs the masses
A scholar who deliberately distorts scripture for worldly gain
A person who follows a prophet without seeking evidence
questions.explanation: In this ayah, أُمِّيُّونَ refers to the ignorant masses among the Jews (جُهَّال العَوَام) who could neither read nor write and had no direct access to the Torah — making them entirely dependent on whatever their rabbis told them.

questions.question: What are أَمَانِيُّ (amaniyy, sing. أُمْنِيَّة) as described in the tafseer of Ayah 78?
options: False wishful thinking and baseless hopes instilled in the masses by the rabbis
Solemn covenants recorded in the Torah and binding upon the Jewish community
Intercession requests that the masses made to their prophets and ancestors
The authentic rulings of the Tawrat that the rabbis faithfully taught
questions.explanation: The أَمَانِيُّ were fabricated hopes fed to the Jewish masses — e.g., that the Fire would only touch them for a few days, that their prophets would intercede for them, that they were the beloved (ahibba') of Allah — none grounded in the actual Tawrat.

questions.question: What does بَلَى (balā) mean and what does it do in Ayah 81?
options: It means 'perhaps' — introducing uncertainty about the nature of the Jews' punishment
It means 'and' — connecting Allah's warning to the covenant already mentioned
It means 'except' — carving out a special exception for those who repent
It means 'yes/indeed' — it negates the Jews' false claim and affirms the true reality
questions.explanation: بَلَى is a response particle that negates a preceding negative (or false) claim and affirms the truth that follows — here it directly refutes the claim that the Fire will barely touch them, and introduces the real condition for eternal punishment.

questions.question: What is the Hanafi ruling on بِنَاء (bana) — continuing salah from the point of interruption after wudu breaks?
options: It is never permitted; salah must always be restarted from the beginning
It is permitted for the imam only, not for a muqtadi praying behind him
It is permitted only when the hadas requires ghusl (major purification)
It is permitted under 13 conditions, provided the hadas was involuntary
questions.explanation: The Hanafi position holds bana is valid when all 13 conditions are met, the first being that the hadas was involuntary. If wudu was broken deliberately, bana is not permitted and the salah must be restarted.

questions.question: What are the three absolute prohibition times during which no salah of any kind — Fard, Nafil, Qada, Janazah, or Sajda-e-Tilawat — may be performed?
options: Between Fajr and Dhuhr, between Dhuhr and Asr, and between Asr and Maghrib
During the final third of the night, at noon, and immediately before Fajr
At sunrise, at sunset, and when the sun is exactly at its zenith (Zawal/Istiwa')
After the Fajr iqamah, after the Asr iqamah, and at midnight
questions.explanation: The three absolute Makruh Tahrimi times are: طُلُوع الشَّمْس (sunrise), غُرُوب الشَّمْس (sunset), and الاسْتِوَاء (the exact midday zenith). At these times all forms of salah — including Janazah and Sajda-e-Tilawat — are prohibited.

questions.question: According to the Hanafi madhab, when does Tartib (the obligation to pray qada prayers in their original order) drop?
options: As soon as a person misses one prayer without a valid excuse
When the number of missed prayers reaches three
When the number of missed prayers exceeds five — i.e., when the sixth becomes fully qada
When a person has been unconscious for more than a day and a night
questions.explanation: Tartib is Wajib for a Sahib al-Tartib (one with five or fewer missed prayers). The Mufta bihi position is that Tartib drops when the sixth prayer's time fully expires — making six prayers completely qada.

questions.question: In the Hanafi ruling on the Qa'dah Akhirah, what happens if a worshipper deliberately breaks wudu after completing the tashahud duration in the final sitting?
options: The salah is considered complete, though he should ideally return and make taslim
The salah is suspended until wudu is made; he must then repeat the entire final rak'ah
Only the final sitting must be repeated; the preceding rak'at remain valid
The salah is completely void (batil) and must be restarted from the beginning
questions.explanation: Once the fundamental arkan of salah are fulfilled in the final qa'dah, even deliberate violations do not nullify the salah. The worshipper's salah is considered complete; returning and making taslim is the proper way to close it.

questions.question: Who is a صَاحِب التَّرْتِيب (Sahib al-Tartib) in Hanafi fiqh?
options: A person upon whom five or fewer qada (missed) prayers are currently outstanding
A person who has never missed a prayer in their life
A person who has memorized the Quran and regularly leads congregational prayer
A person who arranges and straightens the rows in congregational prayer
questions.explanation: Sahib al-Tartib is a person with five or fewer outstanding missed (qada) prayers. For such a person, Tartib — praying them in their original order before the current prayer — is Wajib in the Hanafi madhab.

questions.question: Which description correctly identifies قَهْقَهَة (qahlaqah) during salah?
options: Any involuntary sound made during salah — breaks salah but not wudu
Moderate laughter audible only to the person themselves
A silent smile — no effect on salah or wudu
Loud laughter audible to those praying nearby — breaks both salah and wudu
questions.explanation: قَهْقَهَة is the loudest type of laughter during salah — audible to those nearby — and it breaks both salah (making it batil) and wudu. This distinguishes it from Tabassum (a silent smile, no effect) and the moderate Qahqah (heard only by oneself).

questions.question: What is اسْتِخْلَاف (istikhlaf) in the context of salah?
options: Performing salah by gestures when unable to complete the full physical postures
Making up a missed prayer from a previous day in the correct sequence
The act of the imam giving taslim to formally conclude the congregation's salah
Appointing a qualified substitute imam to lead the congregation when the original imam must withdraw
questions.explanation: الاسْتِخْلَاف is appointing a qualified substitute imam mid-salah — for example, when the original imam's wudu breaks and he must leave. The substitute leads to completion; the original imam, upon returning, rejoins as a muqtadi.
